match_note: The first-round reports describe content present in arXiv v1. That includes the kz broadening of ~0.4 Å^-1 that R1 quotes from the v1 text and Methods III D (note that the v1 Fig. 3 caption already says 0.2 Å^-1). It also includes the surface-doping estimate from the fitted Fermi-pocket area (p≈0.22, Supp. VI F), a single 100 meV Gaussian Anderson-disorder strength, AFM-derived edge roughness plus the GE0.5 probabilistic model, and the self-consistent BdG nearest-neighbour pairing with no description of how d-wave symmetry is implemented. The revised passages quoted in the rebuttal replace v1 text: the Fourier width changes from 2/λ to 1/λ, the doping estimate changes from p=0.2271 to 0.19, and the Supplement adds sections on disorder strengths and realizations, AFM statistics, core levels and a thin metallic layer. This confirms that the reviewed version is v1.

concerns.quote: The absence of a superconducting gap in the ARPES spectra could in principle arise from a deviation in surface doping rather than intrinsic pair-breaking effects.
concerns.summary: The missing gap could be caused by a surface carrier concentration that differs from the bulk, rather than by pair breaking or disorder.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: In Fig. 3b, the experimentally determined Fermi surface does not appear to quantitatively match the simulated one in terms of enclosed volume... a quantitative and transparent analysis is not presented.
concerns.summary: The measured Fermi surface volume does not match the simulated contour, and the Luttinger-count doping estimate is not presented transparently.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: It is important to establish that the (110) surface remains sufficiently clean and free from adsorbates during the measurement. In this regard, additional evidence such as shallow core-level spectroscopy would be helpful.
concerns.summary: Flatness does not prove cleanliness, so the authors should show, for example with shallow core-level spectra, that the 6 K surface is free of adsorbates.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: a discussion of possible surface aging effects would strengthen confidence in the reliability of the spectra.
concerns.summary: The authors should discuss possible time-dependent surface aging during the measurement.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the measured spectra may contain contributions from a wide range of momenta, including near-nodal regions where the superconducting gap is small or vanishing. Such mixing could effectively mask the superconducting gap
concerns.summary: The large kz broadening (~0.4 Å^-1) could mix near-nodal spectral weight into antinodal cuts and hide the gap, independent of pair breaking or disorder.

concerns.quote: it would be useful to clarify whether this effect is fully captured in the simulations, and to what extent it may affect the visibility of the superconducting gap.
concerns.summary: The authors should clarify whether the simulations fully include kz broadening and how much it reduces gap visibility.

concerns.quote: the possible effects of surface instabilities, time-reversal symmetry breaking, phase-crystal formation or edge magnetism on the flat-band spectral weight and ARPES visibility are only limitedly discussed.
concerns.summary: Competing surface orders (TRSB, phase crystal, mixed parity, edge magnetism) are not weighed as alternative explanations for the missing flat-band peak.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the possible influence of microscopic domain or facet structures on the flat-band spectral weight could be discussed more explicitly.
concerns.summary: The authors should discuss more explicitly how interface states, facet mixtures or microscopic domains could affect flat-band spectral weight.

concerns.quote: the generality and conclusiveness of the present interpretation would benefit from a more balanced discussion of alternative scenarios and a clearer statement of the limitations of the calculations.
concerns.summary: The manuscript should state the limitations of the BdG calculations more clearly and temper how general the disorder interpretation is claimed to be.

concerns.quote: results for several representative disorder strengths such as 20meV 50meV and 100meV would help clarify whether the suppression of the flat-band peak depends sensitively on a particular disorder scale
concerns.summary: Only 100 meV disorder is shown, so a sweep of disorder strength is needed to test how robust the flat-band suppression is.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: spatially smooth or extended disorder may produce weaker scattering between opposite chirality sectors than short-range onsite disorder and may therefore suppress the flat-band peak less strongly than in the present calculation.
concerns.summary: Uncorrelated onsite Gaussian disorder may not represent LSCO's real disorder landscape and may overestimate the flat-band suppression.

concerns.quote: The manuscript does not specify how many disorder configurations were used whether the results were averaged or how large the variation between realizations is.
concerns.summary: It is unclear whether the disorder spectra are a single realization or an ensemble average, and realization-to-realization variation is not reported.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: the spectral function is not systematically examined as a function of roughness autocorrelation length or high-frequency components.
concerns.summary: The roughness analysis relies on RMS amplitude and does not systematically examine lateral correlation length or high-frequency components.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: it would be useful to compare how edge-local onsite disorder and bulk-distributed disorder differently affect the flat-band peak and how bulk disorder is projected onto the surface spectral weight.
concerns.summary: The separate contributions of edge-localized and bulk-distributed disorder to flat-band suppression are not distinguished.
concerns.response: addressed with new data or analysis

concerns.quote: it is unclear whether the relative sign between the x-bond and y-bond pairing amplitudes is imposed only through the initial condition whether the d-wave symmetry is explicitly constrained during the self-consistency loop
concerns.summary: The implementation of d-wave symmetry in the self-consistent BdG loop needs a clearer description for reproducibility.

later_concerns.quote: the final sentence of the Abstract remains somewhat stronger than the evidence warrants. I encourage the authors to consider a modest softening of this wording
later_concerns.summary: The Abstract overstates disorder as the key factor; the calculations show it is a sufficient mechanism, not that it is the unique cause.

first_round.quote: I believe that several technical issues should be clarified before the manuscript can be accepted... I would be happy to recommend publication after the above concerns are adequately addressed.
I do not think the manuscript is ready for publication in its present form. I would recommend publication only after major revision addressing the issues raised above.

recommendations.note: First round is Version 0 of a Nature Communications peer review file. There is no sign of a transfer from another journal, and no referee co-signs another's report. R1 gives no explicit category, so the rating is inferred. The tone is positive and the requests are framed as clarifications. R1 is borderline between minor and major, because it also asks for a quantitative Fermi-surface volume extraction, possible core-level spectra, an aging discussion and a kz-broadening analysis. R2 explicitly requests major revision. In round two both referees recommended publication.
recommendations.label: contested
